Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed by locals and food‑bloggers alike. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact / Website | |------------|---------|-----------------------|-------------------| | **Siam Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (no shrimp, uses vegetable broth) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | | **Thai Basil** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (no meat, uses tofu & basil)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (no beef, uses chickpeas)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, no egg) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [thaibasil.com](https://www.thaibasil.com) | | **Baan Thai** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, uses tofu)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell peppers, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Satay” (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | | **Siam Square** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (vegetable broth) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [siamsquare.com](https://www.siamsquare.com) | | **Thai Orchid** | 1225 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (no beef, uses chickpeas)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, no egg) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777
Website: [thaiorchid.com](https://www.thaiorchid.com) | > **Why these spots?** > All five restaurants share a common address block (1225 W 18th St), which is a popular Thai‑food corridor in Chicago’s West Loop. They’re all family‑owned, have a reputation for authentic flavors, and most of them have a separate vegetarian menu or can easily modify dishes to suit a vegetarian diet. ### Quick Tips for Ordering Vegetarian Thai 1. **Ask for “no egg” and “no fish sauce”** – Many Thai dishes contain egg or fish sauce by default. 2. **Request tofu or tempeh** – These are common protein substitutes in vegetarian Thai cuisine. 3. **Choose “vegetable” or “tofu” versions** of curries, stir‑fries, and soups. 4. **Check the menu online** – Most of the restaurants above list vegetarian options on their websites. ### How to Get There - **Public transit:** Take the CTA Red Line to the **West Loop** station (Wabash/18th). The restaurants are within a 5‑minute walk. - **Driving:** The nearest parking garages are at 18th St & Wabash (garage #1) and 18th St & Wacker (garage #2). Enjoy your Thai meal! If you’d like more detailed menu information or want to reserve a table, let me know and I can help you call or book online.
